The right to vote is enshrined in the US Constitution, and it is a right and a privilege for all those who are citizens to exercise! So, it shouldn't come as a surprise to anyone that we need to screen our Texas voter roll against non-citizens voting in our elections, and in this front page story by Jeremy Wallace, “GOP plans a push for purge of voter rolls,” —- https://www.houstonchronicle.com/politics/texas/article/Here-comes-another-Texas-voter-purge-but-this-16464794.php —- explains what in SB 1 was changed to do this comparison correctly in the future, as maintaining a voter roll with integrity is paramount to having election results both the candidates and the public can trust!

Basically, the bill sets up guidelines on citizenship cross checks using DPS data of the type I advocated for 15 years ago as Harris County Voter Registrar to the Federal Congress. You see, the "Feds" could have provided a citizenship list for decades if they wanted to, but we are the largest nation on Earth without one...

Therefore, it's up to the Texas Secretary of State Elections Division to use the DPS data correctly, and yes, to begin a "purge" process of voter rolls with local election officials giving the voter a chance to respond to the letter. This happens every two years by federal law - a "purge" of those voters who have moved or died, etc... and is not some "Draconian," "Republican" operation, but one that should happen in every state in the union by federal law, NVRA, HAVA, the Real ID Act, and now in Texas with the passage of SB 1!

When I first got the Voter Registrar job in 1998 in Harris County as Tax Assessor-Collector, there were 50k deceased and felon registrations on the voter roll - 1% of them were voting! If we hadn't cleaned up these registrations, 500 of them could have decided the presidential election in 2000 like they did in Florida. It's why I was Senator Hughes's 1st co-author on SB 1, as I knew how bad the voter rolls can be from actual experience! --- Sen. PB.

- Up to $2,500 a month in rent and utility arrears going back to March 2020.
- Up to $2,000 for future rent payments.
- Up to $500 a month for future electric, water and sewer, and gas bills.
- For future payments, a household must requalify every three months and funds must be available. A household will need income and tax documents to requalify. 
- Total length of rent and utility help is 12 months per household.
